fullPassage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.

Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an (A)[illustrator / instructor]. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in (B)[comparison / competition]. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was (C)[embarrassed / encouraged] because it wasn't very good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 고등학교에서 모두가 내가 얼마나 재능 있는 예술가인지 말해서 삽화가가 되는 꿈을 꾸었다. 그러나 대학에서는 모두가 훨씬 더 재능 있어 보였고, 너무 열심히 해서 비교하면 작게 느껴졌다. 어느 날 중학교 때 상 받은 그림을 보고 부끄러웠다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① illustrator — comparison — embarrassed
❌ ② instructor — comparison — encouraged
❌ ③ illustrator — competition — embarrassed
❌ ④ instructor — competition — encouraged
✅ (A) illustrator: 예술가가 되고 싶어 삽화가를 꿈꿈. instructor(강사)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (B) comparison: 'felt small in comparison'은 '비교하면 작게 느낌'. competition(경쟁)은 부자연스러움. ✅ (C) embarrassed: 그림이 별로라서 부끄러움. encouraged(격려받은)는 반대 의미.
det.tip: comparison vs competition: 비교 vs 경쟁. 'in comparison'은 '비교하면'이라는 관용 표현.

questions.passage: Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me (A)[swallowed / followed] my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly (B)[heated / repeated] conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking (C)[risks / notes], I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 내 안의 작은 블랙홀이 발언을 고려할 때 내 목소리를 삼켜버렸다. 특히 격렬한 대화 후 스스로에게 물었다. 다른 사람들이 위험을 감수하는 것을 보고 나도 해야겠다고 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① swallowed — heated — risks
❌ ② followed — heated — notes
❌ ③ swallowed — repeated — notes
❌ ④ followed — repeated — risks
✅ (A) swallowed: 블랙홀이 목소리를 '삼킴'은 비유적 표현. followed(따라감)는 어색. ✅ (B) heated: 'heated conversation'은 '격렬한 대화'. repeated(반복된)는 맥락 불일치. ✅ (C) risks: 'taking risks'는 '위험을 감수함'. taking notes(필기)는 문맥과 무관.
det.tip: swallow: '삼키다' → 비유적으로 '억누르다'. heated: '뜨거운' → 비유적으로 '격렬한'.

questions.passage: I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of (A)[influence / reference], and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of (B)[concern / confidence]: things I worry about but have no direct control over. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly (C)[exhausted / excited]. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 기사는 두 원을 그리라고 했다. 작은 원은 영향력의 원. 큰 원은 걱정의 원: 걱정하지만 통제할 수 없는 것들. 모든 것이 영향력의 원에 있다고 믿으면 스트레스받고 항상 지침.
det.analysis:
✅ ① influence — concern — exhausted
❌ ② reference — concern — excited
❌ ③ influence — confidence — exhausted
❌ ④ reference — confidence — excited
✅ (A) influence: 'circle of influence'는 본문의 핵심 개념. reference(참조)는 개념과 무관. ✅ (B) concern: 'circle of concern'은 걱정하지만 통제 불가한 영역. confidence(자신감)는 반대 뉘앙스. ✅ (C) exhausted: 모든 것을 통제하려 하면 '지침'. excited(신남)는 문맥 반대.
det.tip: influence(영향력) vs concern(걱정): Stephen Covey의 '영향력의 원/걱정의 원' 개념. exhausted = extremely tired.

questions.passage: ①<u>People</u> say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. ②<u>That</u>'s why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. ③<u>Maybe</u> they had an <u>advantage</u>, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are ④<u>going</u> to compare yourself to anyone, the only <u>fair</u> comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much <u>effort</u> you've put in. It is <u>discouraging</u> to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사과를 오렌지에 비교하면 안 된다고 하고, 그 말이 맞다. 자신을 인터넷 유명인이나 주변 사람과 비교하는 것은 의미가 없다. 유일하게 공정한 비교 대상은 '어제의 나'이다. 내가 발전한 모습을 보는 것은 힘이 나는(empowering) 일이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①advantage(이점): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②fair(공정한): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③effort(노력): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④discouraging(낙담하게 하는): 원문은 empowering(힘이 나는). 발전을 보는 것은 긍정적이므로 discouraging은 부적절.
det.tip: empowering(힘을 주는) ↔ discouraging(낙담시키는). 문맥이 긍정적이면 긍정 어휘가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: So I ①<u>left</u> my comfort zone and started to speak up. I ②<u>grew</u> <u>intellectually</u> and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got <u>③<u>closer</u></u> to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I ④<u>have</u> more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely <u>rewarding</u> in <u>predictable</u> ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 안전지대를 떠나 발언하기 시작했다. 지적으로, 사회적으로 성장했다. 친구들과 더 가까워졌다. 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것은 예상치 못한(unexpected) 방식으로 보람 있을 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①intellectually(지적으로): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②closer(더 가까이): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③rewarding(보람 있는): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④predictable(예측 가능한): 원문은 unexpected(예상치 못한). 위험 감수의 보상이 '예측 가능'하면 문맥 모순.
det.tip: unexpected(예상치 못한) ↔ predictable(예측 가능한). 위험 감수 → 예상 밖의 보상이 핵심 메시지.

questions.passage: I ①<u>would</u> get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, <u>mediate</u> a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was ②<u>drowning</u> in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties. The ③<u>article</u> advised me to draw two big circles. By <u>④<u>wasting</u></u> less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to <u>invest</u> more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I <u>neglect</u> my own actions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과제 보고서, 친구 사이 중재, 온라인 일지 댓글 때문에 지쳤다. 걱정의 원에 에너지를 덜 낭비함으로써 중요한 것에 더 투자할 수 있었다. 더 이상 친구들 생각을 걱정하지 않고 내 행동에 집중한다(focus on).
det.analysis: ✅ ①mediate(중재하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②wasting(낭비하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③invest(투자하다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④neglect(무시하다): 원문은 focus on(집중하다). 에너지를 행동에 '무시한다'는 반대 의미.
det.tip: focus on(~에 집중하다) ↔ neglect(무시하다, 소홀히 하다). 걱정의 원에서 영향력의 원으로 에너지를 전환하는 것이 핵심.

questions.passage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was ____ because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.

Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대학에서 비교하며 작게 느꼈다. 중학교 때 상 받은 그림을 보았는데 별로여서 부끄러웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②embarrassed: 그림이 'wasn't very good'이므로 부끄러움이 적절. ❌ ①delighted(기뻐함): 별로인 그림에 기쁨은 어색. ❌ ③relieved(안도함): 안도할 맥락 없음. ❌ ④indifferent(무관심한): 감정 묘사와 불일치.
det.tip: embarrassed: 부끄러운. '별로 좋지 않았기 때문에' → 부끄러움이 자연스러운 감정.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수업 토론에서 의견을 말하는가, 침묵하는가? 발언을 고려할 때 블랙홀이 목소리를 삼켰다. 조롱당하거나 틀릴 결과가 항상 걱정이었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ridiculed: 'being wrong'과 병렬로 발언의 부정적 결과. 조롱당할까 봐 두려움. ❌ ①praised(칭찬받음): 발언을 두려워하는 맥락과 불일치. ❌ ②ignored(무시됨): 가능하나 'being wrong'과의 병렬에서 ridiculed가 더 적절. ❌ ④promoted(승진됨): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: ridicule: 조롱하다. 발언 두려움의 핵심은 '틀리거나 조롱당할까 봐'.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>happened</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 'progress'와 (B)에서 사용된 'worked through'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 다른 사람과만 비교할 때 내 능력의 발전을 볼 수 없었다. (B) 2학년에서 3학년으로 겪어 나가면서 학교와 개인 생활의 균형이 더 어려웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A)progress=발전: 능력이 나아진 정도. (B)worked through=겪어 나가다: 시간을 보내며 경험. ❌ ① (B)해결하다: work through는 여기서 '~을 거쳐 가다'. ❌ ③ (A)진행: 능력의 '진행'보다 '발전'이 적절. ❌ ④ 조합 불일치.
det.tip: progress: ①진행 ②발전. work through: ①해결하다 ②겪어 나가다. 맥락으로 의미 구분.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to feel resentful longing for someone's possessions, advantages, or success"

det.korean: "다른 사람의 소유물, 이점, 또는 성공에 대해 원망 어린 갈망을 느끼다"
det.analysis: ✅ ④envy: 부러워하다, 시기하다. 정의와 정확히 일치. ❌ ①compare(비교하다): 감정이 아닌 행동. ❌ ②invest(투자하다): 무관. ❌ ③participate(참여하다): 무관.
det.tip: envy: 시기, 부러움. 본문 'to envy the success of others'에서 등장. jealousy와 유사하나 envy는 갖고 싶은 마음, jealousy는 빼앗길까 두려운 마음.

다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

He __________ (clear) expressed his opinion in the discussion, and everyone understood his point. (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 그는 토론에서 자신의 의견을 명확하게 표현했고, 모두가 그의 요점을 이해했다.
det.analysis: ✅ clearly: 동사 expressed를 수식하는 부사 형태. clear(형용사) → clearly(부사).

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. The only fair __________ is "yesterday-you."
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

The teacher made a __________ (compare) between the two essays to show the students how to improve. (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 선생님은 학생들에게 개선 방법을 보여주기 위해 두 에세이를 비교했다.
det.analysis: ✅ comparison: 관사 a 뒤이므로 명사 형태. compare(동사) → comparison(명사).
det.tip: compare(동사: 비교하다) → comparison(명사: 비교). 'make a comparison' = '비교하다'. 본문의 'the only fair comparison'에서도 명사로 사용.

questions.passage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수업 토론에서 침묵하곤 했다. 블랙홀이 목소리를 삼켰다. 결국 '무엇이 두렵지?'라고 자문하고 안전지대를 떠나 발언하기 시작했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①comfort zone: '안전지대를 떠나다'는 익숙한 상태에서 벗어나는 것. ❌ ②social circle(사교 모임): 사교 모임을 떠나는 것은 발언 시작과 무관. ❌ ③study group(스터디 그룹): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④daily routine(일상): 일상을 떠나는 것과 발언은 무관.
det.tip: leave one's comfort zone: 안전지대를 벗어나다. 새로운 시도를 할 때 자주 쓰는 표현.

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the amount of research I do for it.
whether my friends approve of me.
how other students perform on the test

det.korean: 기사가 두 원을 그리라고 했다. 작은 원은 영향력의 원(직접 통제 가능), 큰 원은 걱정의 원(걱정하지만 통제 불가). 교수가 보고서에 어떻게 반응할지는 통제 불가이지만, 보고서를 위해 하는 연구의 양은 통제 가능하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③the amount of research I do for it: 원문 그대로. 자기가 통제할 수 있는 노력의 양. ❌ ①what grade I will receive: 성적은 교수가 결정 → 걱정의 원. ❌ ②whether my friends approve: 타인의 승인 → 걱정의 원. ❌ ④how other students perform: 다른 학생 성적 → 걱정의 원.
det.tip: circle of influence vs circle of concern: 내가 통제 가능한 것(행동, 노력) vs 불가능한 것(타인 반응, 결과).
